name: Canadian wildfire smoke
rarityNote: Canada's worst fire season on record; nothing in the 2022–2026 record matches this smoke over the US north-east. Draft: verify.

peak.note: Highest 2023-06 monthly-mean pm2_5 cell in the footprint (+150 km), CAMS via Open-Meteo.

areaKm2.note: Footprint cells at or above twice their own median over the record.

reachKm.note: Greatest distance from the source point to such a cell.

clues.riddle: Dry thunderstorms lit a forest, and a city to the south turned orange.

questions.prompt: What started most of the fires behind this smoke?
options: Fires spreading north from the United States
Controlled burns that got out of hand
questions.explanation: A cluster of dry thunderstorms on 1 June lit more than 30 fires across western Quebec after an unusually dry spring.

questions.prompt: Why did New York's sky turn orange in early June 2023?
options: Smoke from wildfires in the US
Industrial smog trapped over the city
Smoke from Quebec carried south on northerly winds
Dust blown in from the Sahara
questions.explanation: More than 150 fires were burning in Quebec on 6 June, and northerly winds carried their smoke hundreds of kilometres south.

back: After an unusually dry spring, dry thunderstorms on 1 June lit dozens of fires in Quebec's boreal forest; within a week more than 150 were burning.
Northerly winds pushed the smoke south over Ontario and the US north-east, and on 7 June New York's sky turned orange.
actual: The smoke came from Quebec, hundreds of kilometres north.

name: Indonesian peat haze
rarityNote: The highest September in the 2022–2026 record, 2.4× the 2023 haze year. Draft: compare with 2015 and 2019 before calling it rare.

peak.note: Highest 2026-09 monthly-mean pm2_5 cell in the footprint (+150 km), CAMS via Open-Meteo.

areaKm2.note: Footprint cells at or above twice their own median over the record.

reachKm.note: Greatest distance from the source point to such a cell.

clues.riddle: Ground that burns from below fills a strait with smoke.

questions.prompt: Where did Singapore's haze in September 2026 come from?
options: Fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan, carried on the wind
Ships in the Strait of Malacca
questions.explanation: Singapore's environment agency detected numerous hotspots across Kalimantan and central and southern Sumatra, where dense smoke had hung since late August.

questions.prompt: Why is peat haze so hard to put out?
options: Lightning relights the fires every day
Drained peat smoulders underground, where rain rarely reaches it
questions.explanation: Peat is old, waterlogged plant matter. Drained for plantations it dries out, and once lit it smoulders below the surface for weeks.
questions.source: Page et al., Nature 420, 61–65 (2002), on Indonesia's 1997 peat fires

back: Fires in drained peatland across Kalimantan and southern Sumatra filled the region with smoke from late August. Drained peat dries out and smoulders underground for weeks, so rain rarely puts it out.
Winds carried the smoke to Singapore and Malaysia; on 4 September Singapore's air reached the unhealthy range for the first time since 2023.
actual: The smoke is carried in from fires hundreds of kilometres away.

name: North Indian and Pakistani smog
rarityNote: Every November; 2024 was the worst of the four in the record.

peak.note: Highest 2024-11 monthly-mean pm2_5 cell in the footprint (+150 km), CAMS via Open-Meteo.

areaKm2.note: Footprint cells at or above twice their own median over the record.

reachKm.note: Greatest distance from the source point to such a cell.

region: Punjab, Haryana and the Gangetic plain

clues.riddle: After the rice harvest, the plain fills with smoke and cold air holds it down.

questions.prompt: What drives most of this month-long November haze?
options: Crop stubble burning plus local pollution, held down by cold still air
questions.explanation: Farm fires in Punjab and Haryana add a large share on peak days, by Delhi's Decision Support System over a third on some days; the rest is the region's own traffic, industry and dust, held near the ground by cold, still air.
questions.source: CSE, citing Delhi DSS daily estimates: https://www.cseindia.org/cse-in-news?page=339

questions.prompt: Where is the November haze densest in this record?
questions.explanation: In the November 2024 monthly mean the highest cell sits in Pakistani Punjab; the haze covers both sides of the border.
questions.source: CAMS monthly mean PM2.5, November 2024, as shown in this atlas

back: After the rice harvest, farmers in Punjab and Haryana, and in Pakistani Punjab, burn the leftover stubble to clear their fields.
Cold, still November air traps that smoke together with the region's traffic, industry and dust across the whole plain.
actual: Fireworks add a night or two; the month-long smog is crop smoke and local pollution held down by winter air.
sources: Govardhan et al., Geosci. Model Dev. 17, 2617 (2024)
